learningObjective: Distinguish per-tensor, per-channel, and per-group quantization by scale/zero-point count and hardware/kernel implications.

canonicalClaims.claim: Quantization granularity ranges from one (scale, zero-point) per tensor to one per (channel, group) tile: per-tensor is cheapest but least accurate; per-channel adds negligible epilogue cost with better fit; per-group (typical group_size 128) is standard for W4A16 kernels balancing accuracy and metadata.
conditions: The kernel is designed for the chosen granularity (per-tensor kernels cannot consume per-group scales).
Metadata storage is accounted for in the memory budget.
nonImplications: Does not imply finer granularity is always better; smaller groups add metadata that can offset accuracy gains.
Does not imply the same granularity must be used for weights and activations.

misconceptions.claim: Per-tensor quantization is strictly more accurate than per-channel because Tensor Cores run at peak with a single scale.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-tensor forces one scale for heterogeneous channels, degrading accuracy; per-channel adds epilogue math but is not throughput-limited by scale handling.

misconceptions.claim: Per-group quantization is illegal because a dot product cannot mix multiple scales.
misconceptions.whyWrong: W4A16 kernels perform grouped partial accumulation: accumulate within a group, apply group scale, then combine — a standard pattern in GPTQ/AWQ kernels.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: GPTQ / AWQ kernel implementations (e.g., ExLlama, Marlin)

misconceptions.claim: Per-channel scales must always be per-input-channel (columns of W).
misconceptions.whyWrong: For a `[out, in]` weight, per-output-channel (per-row) is more common because it allows fused into the epilogue; per-input-channel would require per-K-step handling.

misconceptions.claim: Group size is arbitrary and does not affect kernel design.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Group size must divide the K-axis tile of the GEMM kernel; typical values are 32, 64, 128 aligned with kernel tile sizes.

implementationFacts: AWQ uses group_size = 128 as its default.
TensorRT default weight quantization: symmetric per-channel INT8.
Per-group INT4 GEMMs on GPU: Marlin, ExLlama, gptq_gemm variants.
performanceScenarios: For a 4096×4096 weight matrix, per-tensor uses 2 scalars; per-channel uses 4096; per-group (128) uses 4096×32 = 131072 scalars — still tiny compared to the weight itself.
